name: charity: water
mission: charity: water is a nonprofit organization bringing clean and safe drinking water to people in developing countries. The organization inspires giving and empowers others to fundraise for sustainable water solutions. 100% of public donations are sent to local partners on the ground, who build and implement the projects. When the projects are completed, charity: water proves every one of them using GPS coordinates, photos and details of the community served.

theoryOfChange: Charity Water utilizes a 'MAP Framework' which is a monitoring and evaluation framework designed to collect data across various water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) indicators. This framework helps them understand the impact of funded projects, maximize effectiveness, and guide future funding decisions. The MAP Framework includes two types of data collection: Annual Check-ins (household surveys at baseline and endline of a grant) and Post-Implementation Monitoring (a comprehensive assessment of past work every few years). The framework aims to answer questions about immediate improvements, sustained access, and reasons for water point functionality issues.

rich_narrative.summary: charity: water is a global humanitarian organization dedicated to ending the water crisis by providing clean and safe drinking water to communities in extreme poverty. Founded in <cite id="2">2006</cite>, the organization has scaled its operations to fund over <cite id="6">197,000 water projects</cite> across Africa and Asia. The charity maintains an exceptional <cite id="1">100/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting its commitment to transparency and financial health. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="11">$96,818,300 in total revenue</cite>, which supports a diverse range of technical solutions including <cite id="5">drilled wells, piped systems, and BioSand filters</cite>. A defining feature of their model is the "100% promise," where private donors cover all operating costs, allowing public donations to go directly to water projects. This efficiency is evidenced by a <cite id="1">fundraising efficiency of $0.11 per $1 raised</cite>, which is significantly better than many industry peers. While the organization is <cite id="8">SADAQAH-ELIGIBLE</cite> and does not currently offer a specific zakat-verified pathway, its work in Muslim-majority regions like <cite id="6">Malawi and Uganda</cite> provides a strong humanitarian alignment for faith-based donors looking to support sustainable infrastructure in underserved areas.
